Subject: Intro: telemetry & evals at FinLytics

Hi Rishi / team,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can move toward an internal evaluation:

Pain points we discussed:
- We have unpredictable token spend spikes on customer-facing assistants when new prompts are published.
- We lack deterministic drift/regression detection after model or prompt changes — currently we find regressions by customer reports.
- No good request-level tracing to connect an assistant response back to the specific prompt variants and model version.
- Our data-retention and audit requirements mean we need per-request audit logs for at least 90 days.

Current stack and constraints:
- Front end -> AWS Lambda -> calls to OpenAI hosted endpoints; some on-prem pre-processing.
- Lightweight internal metrics in Datadog but no token-level breakdowns or golden prompt comparisons.
- Security: SOC2 in progress, mandatory vendor questionnaire for vendor onboarding happens next quarter.

Success criteria for a PoC:
1) Ability to surface a per-route dashboard with token cost broken down by prompt variant and model version.
2) Tracing hooks to tag requests with prompt variant id + customer id and replay traces for investigations.
3) Automated regression alerts if golden-prompt throughput or correctness drops > 5% post-deploy.
4) Rollout guardrails (canary + automatic rollback or traffic cut) tied to regression signals.

Immediate asks:
- Can you share a short template of the dashboard you’d propose?
- Please send an example golden prompt set and any data-format requirements for evaluating regressions.
- Rough estimate on required changes to our runtime (we prefer minimal instrumentation).

I attached our current telemetry diagram (finlytics-current-telemetry-stack.pdf). We also have a short internal window next week for a tech-deep dive (prefer mornings PT).

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Williams
Product Lead, FinLytics

Hi Sara — really useful notes, thanks for writing these up. Below is a short post-call recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Recap (what we heard)
- Token-cost visibility required at prompt-variant + model-version granularity.
- Need tracing hooks to link each request to a variant id and model version, plus a replay capability for investigation.
- Guardrails and automated regression detection for prompt/model rollouts.
- Compliance requirement: 90-day audit logs and clear evidence for vendor questionnaire.

What Redwood can deliver for the PoC
- Per-route dashboards showing: tokens per request, tokens per prompt variant, top cost drivers, and per-customer cost attribution. (We’ll share a mock dashboard link.)
- Tracing hooks: a small SDK snippet to add a prompt_variant_id + model_version tag per request. We store lightweight KV traces that can be replayed for debugging.
- Evals: we run golden-prompt comparisons against a seed set and surface regression alerts when correctness metrics fall below your thresholds.
- Rollout guardrails: canary traffic split + automated rollback if regression alert fires during canary window.

Suggested success criteria for the PoC (aligning to yours):
1) Dashboard populated with 7 days of sampled traffic and token breakdown per variant.
2) Tracing enabled on one customer route and replay validated by your SRE.
3) Regression alert triggers in a controlled test using seeded failing prompts.
4) Documented minimal instrumentation steps for your engineers.

Action items / next steps
- Rishi (me): will upload a CSV with a starter golden-prompt seed and a mock dashboard screenshot: attached as golden_prompts_seed.csv.
- FinLytics (Sara): please confirm one customer route to instrument and share a short sample of ~100 prompts/utterances.
- Monica (CS): can we schedule a 60-min tech deep-dive the week of Jun 1? Monica — please propose 2 slots.
- Ben (solutions): will prepare an outline of any runtime wrapper changes; aim for < 6 hours of engineering for the PoC.

Security & compliance note
- We’ll include SOC2 evidence and our vendor questionnaire answers in the demo workspace. If you prefer, we can sign an NDA prior to sharing detailed telemetry dumps.
